subtitle: On the Frontier of Two Worlds

panels.shot: split-diagonal composition, one half a fortified hill-city above a river, the other a winter steppe camp of cavalry under a crescent moon
panels.action: Jayapala Shahi stands in ornate mail on a battlement above Waihind’s river plain, facing across the frame toward Mahmud of Ghazni in winter furs amid a ring of horsemen and tents in the snow-dusted steppe.

dialogue.text: A court secretary of Ghazni claimed to see it all: the day Jayapala Shahi’s frontier shattered and Mahmud of Ghazni’s road into Hindustan truly opened.

i18n.hi: ग़ज़नी के दरबार लेखक ने दावा किया: उसने सब देखा — जिस दिन जयपाल शाहि की सरहद टूटी और महमूद ग़ज़नी की हिंदुस्तान की राह सच‑मुच खुल गई।

panels.shot: wide aerial sweep over rugged mountains falling into a green plain, a narrow pass like a scar between them
panels.action: The image shows the stony jaws of the Khyber Pass opening onto rich alluvial plains, with faint caravans threading the defile and, in the distance, a fortified town near a winding river.

dialogue.text: For generations, the Hindu Shahi kings watched the Khyber, the stone gate between the highlands of Ghazni and the river plains of Punjab. Their hill forts taxed caravans and checked raiding horsemen.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ियों से हिन्दू शाहि राजा ख़ैबर पर नज़र रखते थे — पत्थर का दरवाज़ा, जो ग़ज़नी के पहाड़ों को पंजाब की दरियाई मैदानी ज़मीन से जोड़ता था। उनके पहाड़ी क़िले काफ़िलों से कर लेते, लुटेरे घुड़सवारों को रोकते।

panels.shot: medium shot of Jayapala in his hall, low-angle to emphasize age and burden, coins and maps spread before him
panels.action: Jayapala Shahi, grey-bearded yet broad-shouldered, leans over a carved wooden table strewn with palm-leaf documents, rough maps, and freshly minted silver coins bearing his name, courtiers dimly visible behind him.

dialogue.text: Jayapala, last strong ruler of the Shahi line, held this frontier from his capital near the Indus. His coins named him king, but his true power lay in watching roads, rivers and tribute flows.

i18n.hi: शाहि वंश के आख़िरी मज़बूत राजा जयपाल ने सिंधु किनारे अपने राजधानी से यह सरहद थामी हुई थी। सिक्कों पर वो राजा था, पर असली ताक़त सड़कों, दरियाओं और नज़राने की निगरानी में थी।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a younger Mahmud in Ghazni’s audience hall, side-lit, with Utbi in shadow nearby holding a scroll
panels.action: Mahmud of Ghazni, in his twenties, sits alert on a low throne in a stone hall hung with banners, one hand resting on his sword-hilt, while a robed secretary with a narrow face clutches a wax tablet at the edge of the scene.

dialogue.text: In Ghazni, young Mahmud inherited a restless cavalry state. His father had pushed toward Khurasan; Mahmud turned his gaze to the east, to the Shahi lands Utbi would later praise as rich, soft and taxable.

i18n.hi: ग़ज़नी में नौजवान महमूद को बेचैन घुड़सवार रियासत मिली। बाप ख़ुरासान की तरफ़ धकेल चुका था; महमूद की नज़र अब पूरब पर थी, उन शाहि इलाकों पर, जिन्हें उत्बी बाद में दौलतमंद, नर्म और कर देने लायक कहेगा।

panels.shot: tight focus on Utbi’s hand writing by lamplight, Mahmud’s silhouette looming behind
panels.action: By the flicker of an oil lamp, the court secretary bends over a parchment, stylus poised, as Mahmud’s shadow falls across the writing surface, hinting at authority shaping the words.

dialogue.text: Utbi, Mahmud’s secretary, later called these campaigns holy war and triumph. But behind his phrases lay colder reasons: restless troops who needed loot, a ruler who needed revenue, and a frontier king seen as a rival.

i18n.hi: उत्बी, महमूद का मुंशी, इन लड़ाइयों को बाद में जिहाद और फ़तह नाम देगा। पर उसके चमकदार जुमलों के पीछे सख़्त वजहें थीं: माल के भूखे सिपाही, ख़ज़ाने को तरसता शहंशाह, और सरहद पर बैठा एक टक्कर का राजा।

panels.shot: winter wide shot of Ghaznavid cavalry column leaving the city, dust and snow mingling
panels.action: Mahmud rides at the head of a long column of mailed horsemen and pack animals, breath steaming in the cold air as they file out of Ghazni’s stone walls into a landscape of frost and rock.

dialogue.text: In the winter of 1001, Mahmud marched through snow and stone, driving his cavalry toward the Shahi frontier. Utbi boasts of speed and surprise; the reality was careful timing before spring melted the passes.

i18n.hi: सन् 1001 की सर्दियों में महमूद बर्फ़ और पत्थरों के बीच से निकला, अपनी सवारी शाहि सरहद की तरफ़ हाँकते हुए। उत्बी रफ़्तार और अचानक धावे के क़िस्से सुनाता है; असलियत थी वक़्त की नापतौल, बसंत से पहले जब दर्रे पिघलने लगते।

panels.shot: medium shot from behind Jayapala on a rampart, looking toward distant dust plumes
panels.action: Jayapala, wrapped in a heavy cloak against the chill, stands on a mud-brick battlement near Waihind, watching faint plumes rise on the horizon as riders bring news across the river plain.

dialogue.text: The Shahi scouts saw the dust first. Jayapala knew this frontier game well: ride out, stall the invader, buy time for allies and for the river to become his shield. He chose battle near Waihind, by the Indus.

i18n.hi: शाहि मुंतज़िमी जासूसों ने पहले धूल देखी। जयपाल इस सरहदी खेल को जानता था: घोड़े चढ़कर आगे बढ़ो, दुश्मन को रोक कर रखो, ताकि यारीदार जुटें और दरिया उसकी ढाल बन जाए। उसने जंग का मैदान वईहिंद, सिंधु किनारे चुना।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of opposing armies deploying on a plain, river and low hills framing them
panels.action: On a cold clear day, the Shahi host with elephants and infantry forms a rough line between low hills and the river, while Mahmud’s lighter cavalry spreads in arcs on the other side, banners stiff in the breeze.

dialogue.text: Utbi paints the Shahi forces as countless and clumsy, Mahmud’s as lean and disciplined. The truth lies between: a frontier king fielding elephants and hill levies against a compact, hardened cavalry army from Ghazni.

i18n.hi: उत्बी शाहि फ़ौज को अनगिनत और सुस्त बताता है, महमूद की सेना को चुस्त और सख़्त। सच बीच में है: एक सरहदी राजा, हाथियों और पहाड़ी पैदल के साथ, ग़ज़नी की सधी, खुरदरी घुड़सवार फ़ौज से भिड़ा।

panels.shot: low-angle close-up on Mahmud mounted, focused, giving a sharp hand signal
panels.action: Mahmud, jaw set, lifts his arm in a brisk signal, his horse stamping as mounted archers around him nock arrows, their faces tense but practised.

dialogue.text: Mahmud used what his steppe and Iranian mentors had taught: fast cavalry, feigned retreats, archery that stung and scattered. Utbi celebrates it as genius; it was also drilled habit, forged in other border wars.

i18n.hi: महमूद ने वही खेल अपनाया जो उसे स्तेपी और ईरानी उस्तादों ने सिखाया था: तेज़ घुड़सवारियाँ, झूठी पीछे हट, तीरंदाज़ी जो चुभे और तितर‑बितर कर दे। उत्बी इसे नायाब अकल लिखता है; दरअस्ल ये बार‑बार की कसरत थी, और सरहदों पर पकी हुई आदत।

panels.shot: wide shot showing Shahi line faltering, elephants turning, cavalry wheeling around them
panels.action: The Shahi line appears in momentary disarray as panicked elephants wheel away from a rain of arrows, dust swirling while Ghaznavid horsemen swing around their flanks in disciplined curves.

dialogue.text: Under the long arc of arrows and sudden cavalry swings, the Shahi line bent. Utbi calls it divine favour; more likely, elephants unnerved by missiles and hill warriors unready for such fluid horse tactics.

i18n.hi: लंबी तीरों की बारिश और अचानक घुड़दौड़ के झूलों के नीचे शाहि क़तारें मुड़ने लगीं। उत्बी इसे ख़ुदा की मदद कहता है; ज़्यादा मुमकिन है तीरों से सहमे हाथी और पहाड़ी जंगजू, जो इतनी लचीली घुड़सवार जंग के लिए तैयार न थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Jayapala surrounded, his horse rearing as Ghaznavid riders close in
panels.action: In the chaos, Jayapala’s horse rears, his face drawn yet resolute as a knot of Ghaznavid riders converges with lances levelled, their circle tightening around him.

dialogue.text: Amid this swirl, Jayapala was unhorsed and taken. Utbi lingers on his capture as proof that the old frontier order was broken in a single stroke. But even here, his is the only detailed voice we have.

i18n.hi: इस अफ़रा‑तफ़री में जयपाल घोड़े से गिरकर क़ैद हो गया। उत्बी उसकी गिरफ़्तारी पर ठहर कर लिखता है, मानो पुराना सरहदी निज़ाम एक ही वार में टूट गया हो। पर सच में हमारे पास उसी की तफ़सील बची है।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a Ghaznavid tent, Jayapala bound yet upright before Mahmud
panels.action: Inside a large campaign tent, Jayapala sits straight-backed despite his bonds, his armour removed but dignity intact, while Mahmud, still in mail, regards him from a simple camp seat; a secretary stands discreetly aside.

dialogue.speaker: jayapala_shahi_and_mahmud_of_ghazni
dialogue.text: “Frontiers fall, but hills remember. My sons still know these roads.”

i18n.hi: "सरहदें गिरती हैं, पहाड़ सब याद रखते हैं। मेरे बेटे अभी भी इन राहों को जानते हैं।"

panels.shot: close-up on Utbi’s face as he watches, eyes intent, then glances to his scroll
panels.action: The secretary’s lined face fills the frame; his eyes flick rapidly between the two rulers before he lowers them to the parchment in his hands, ready to fix what he has seen into an ordered narrative.

dialogue.text: Utbi later wrote of ransoms, pledges and tribute, of chains and humiliation. Archaeology and coins confirm Jayapala’s fall, but not every flourish of Utbi’s pen. His words serve a patron as much as posterity.

i18n.hi: उत्बी बाद में फ़िदये, वादों और नज़राने, ज़ंजीरों और बेइज़्ज़ती के किस्से लिखता है। पुरातत्व और सिक्के जयपाल की हार दिखाते हैं, पर उत्बी के हर रंगीन अल्फ़ाज़ को नहीं। उसकी कलम उतनी ही अपने मालिक की है जितनी आने वाली नस्लों की।

panels.shot: somber medium shot of Jayapala back among his own, head bowed, a pyre structure hinted behind
panels.action: Jayapala stands among a small circle of loyal nobles on a dry hillside, his shoulders heavy, with the wooden frame of a funeral pyre rising behind him and the distant shimmer of the Indus below.

dialogue.text: Later tradition in Persian and Indian sources tells of Jayapala, ashamed by defeat and ransom, choosing death by fire. Whether every detail is true or not, his rule ended soon after; his son Anandapala took the frontier.

i18n.hi: बाद की फ़ारसी और देसी रिवायात बताती हैं कि जयपाल हार और फ़िदये की रुसवाई से जलकर, खुद को आग में झोंक देता है। बारीकियाँ सच्ची हों या नहीं, उसका राज जल्द ही ढह गया; उसका बेटा आनंदपाल सरहद थामने लगा।

panels.shot: insert shot of a Shahi coin being replaced by a Ghaznavid coin on a trader’s weighing scale
panels.action: A merchant’s hand lifts a silver coin bearing Jayapala’s legend from one pan of a scale while placing a Ghaznavid coin on the other, with ledgers and a rolled caravan pass lying nearby.

dialogue.text: Coins tell the quieter story. Shahi mint names give way, over years, to Ghaznavid issues in frontier markets. Control of forts and ferries shifted; Mahmud’s later raids could now bypass what the Shahi hills once guarded.

i18n.hi: सिक्के एक ख़ामोश कहानी कहते हैं। सालों में शाहि टकसाल के नाम मिटते गए, सरहदी बाज़ारों में ग़ज़नवी सिक्के चलने लगे। क़िलों और घाटों का कंट्रोल बदला; अब महमूद के बाद के धावे उन रास्तों से निकल सकते थे, जिन्हें कभी शाहि पहाड़ों ने रोके रखा था।

panels.shot: wide montage-like shot of later Ghaznavid raiding columns crossing rivers and plains, faint overlay of Anandapala rallying
panels.action: A Ghaznavid cavalry column splashes through a broad river at dawn, while in the distance another scene shows Anandapala atop a fort wall rallying spearmen, the two images blended to suggest overlapping years of raid and resistance.

dialogue.text: Jayapala’s defeat did not erase Shahi resistance overnight. Anandapala still fought, forming alliances, holding some hills. Yet the breach of 1001 left a lasting crack; Mahmud’s men now knew the roads and river fords into the plains.

i18n.hi: जयपाल की हार से शाहि जिद एकदम नहीं मिटी। आनंदपाल ने फिर लड़ाई की, यारियाँ जोड़ीं, कुछ पहाड़ थामे रखे। लेकिन 1001 की ये दरार गहरी हो गई; महमूद के सिपाही अब मैदानी इलाकों तक जाने वाली राहों और दरियाई घाटों को पहचानते थे।

panels.shot: present-day style wide shot of the same landscape, empty hills and river, ghostly overlays of Jayapala and Mahmud fading into it
panels.action: The Khyber-Punjab frontier stretches under a calm sky, its hills quiet, the river gleaming, while faint, translucent figures of Jayapala and Mahmud stand facing each other across the landscape, dissolving into earth and sky.

dialogue.text: We remember this battle mostly through Utbi, the secretary who stood near power. His tale must be heard, but weighed against coins, landscapes and other minds, for frontiers are reshaped as much by who writes as by who wins.

i18n.hi: हम इस जंग को ज़्यादातर उत्बी के ज़रिये याद करते हैं — वो मुंशी जो तख़्त के क़रीब खड़ा था। उसकी दास्तान सुननी पड़ती है, पर तौलकर — सिक्कों, ज़मीनों और दूसरी अक़्लों के साथ, क्योंकि सरहदें उतना ही कलम से बदलती हैं, जितना तलवार से।

title_i18n.hi: वो सिपाही-लिखारी जो सब देख रहा था

subtitle_i18n.en: On the Frontier of Two Worlds
